prompt: A black-and-white hand-lettering quote poster in portrait format, flat vector artwork on a solid black background. Five lines of white lettering are stacked in one tight block in the center of the poster, with wide empty black margins around it, and the whole block tilts slightly so each line rises toward the right. At the top, the word "PATIENCE" is written in huge heavy condensed bold sans-serif capitals. Directly beneath it, the word "Builds" is written in large bold flowing brush script with a big looping initial capital. In the middle of the block sits a small solid white rectangular label, and inside that label the word "WHAT" is printed in small bold black sans-serif capitals, with three short white sparkle strokes on each side of the label. Below the label, the word "Hurry" is written in the same bold brush script. At the bottom, the word "BREAKS" is written in the same heavy condensed sans-serif capitals as the top line, and it is the largest line of all. The lines touch and slightly overlap. The poster shows only these five words, each of them once, in pure white and black with no gray, no shadow, no texture, and nothing below the last line.

A black-and-white brush calligraphy poster in portrait format, hand-lettered artwork on a solid black background with a few tiny white star dots. Four lines of white lettering are stacked in one tall block of equal-width lines in the center of the poster, with moderate black margins around it, and the whole block rises slightly to the right. At the top, the word "Brave" is written in flowing connected brush script. Directly beneath it, the word "Hearts" is written in large flowing brush calligraphy script with thick downstrokes, thin upstrokes and looping capitals. Below it, the word "Begin" is written in the same flowing connected brush script as the top line. At the bottom, the word "Again" is written in the same flowing brush calligraphy script. The lines interlock. Large words span the full block width, and small words tuck in beside them. Long ribbon-like swashes curl above the first line and below the last line, and swash tails fill the gaps. The poster shows only these four words, each of them once, in pure white and black with no other colors, no outline, and no other lettering below the last line.
